title: Designing AI To Scale Human Thought — Jun Yu Tan, Tusk
talk_summary: A product-UX talk from Tusk's founding engineer arguing AI should augment rather than automate human work, with three interaction patterns (blind-spot detection, cognitive partnership, proactive guidance) and trust principles. The one concrete, mechanism-level idea is Tusk's PR bug-finding flow: generate candidate tests, actually execute them against the codebase to prove the bug, surface the assumptions made, and let users rate assumptions to tune signal.

takeaways.technique: Prove defects by executing generated tests, not just asserting them
takeaways.what_they_do: On each commit, Tusk generates unit tests for suspected bugs and actually runs them against the codebase/test env, surfacing only issues it can demonstrate will cause problems; users can commit the tests as regression coverage.
takeaways.numbers: verified bugs in 43% of PRs; ~1000 new tests in 2 months

takeaways.technique: Surface the reviewer's assumptions for human/agent adjudication
takeaways.what_they_do: Alongside each finding, Tusk lists the business/engineering assumptions it made and outlines potential fixes, and lets users thumbs-up/down or explain, feeding back into what it flags.
takeaways.evidence_quote: surface any assumptions that task is making be it from a business or engineering standpoint and also outline potential fixes

takeaways.technique: Novelty x criticality triage to cap review noise
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify each suggestion on novelty and criticality: high/high interrupts, low-novelty/high-criticality gives terse standard warnings, low/low is batched and optional; assumes people process only ~3 meaningful suggestions per session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: people tend to only process three or more meaningful suggestions per review session
takeaways.numbers: ~3 meaningful suggestions processed per review session

takeaways.what_they_do: Systematically walk every changed symbol, enumerate what could go wrong including second-order effects up the call stack, rather than free-form review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: systematically look through um every symbol that has been changed finding what could go wrong um consider second order effects in the call stack
